newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-RAIN SAVES INDIA FROM LIKELY DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-RAIN SAVES INDIA FROM LIKELY DEFEAT.

text.p: South African A team opener Louis Koen survived an umpiring error to hit a century against India before rain spared the touring side from the prospect of defeat on Thursday.
India were toiling at 94 for five from 24.2 overs when a downpour ended their faltering chase of South Africa A's 251 for six from 50 overs in the day-night match.

Each side had to receive a minimum of 25 overs for the game to have a result. If a further four balls had been possible to complete the 25th over, India would have had to score 22 more runs for victory.
The touring team made a dreadful start to their run chase against South Africa's combination of emerging youngsters and internationals hoping to fight their way back into the senior team.
Piet Botha dismissed Rahul Dravid and Sunil Joshi with the total seven and when Makhaya Ntini ran out Sachin Tendulkar to make it 75 for four, India's chances looked increasingly slim.
Earlier, Koen scored 105 from 134 balls to help lift his team from 91 for four, with 19-year-old wicketkeeper-batsman Mark Boucher lashing 42 not out from 31 balls in the end-of-innings assault
Koen was dropped at short mid-wicket on 19 and received another let-off on 86 when he was called back from the dressing room by Indian captain Tendulkar.
The third umpire had mistakenly flashed up the red light when he had meant to show green as Koen had made his ground in a run-out appeal.
The mistake was radioed to the on-field umpires and Tendulkar allowed Koen to return from the dressing-room.
India, who have won just one of their 10 matches on tour, meet South Africa in a triangular series match in Port Elizabeth on Sunday.
